findings.title: Exact-case lookup allows blocked addresses to bypass validation
findings.body: The blocked-email lookup compares the supplied address verbatim, and neither BlockedEmail nor User.new_from_params normalizes it. With `blocked@example.com` on the blocklist, registering as `blocked@EXAMPLE.COM` does not find the record, even though email domain names are case-insensitive and this is the same destination. Canonicalize addresses consistently when storing and looking up blocked emails, using the application's email-normalization rules, and test case variants.

findings.title: Concurrent matches lose counter increments
findings.body: `should_block?` reads `match_count`, increments it in Ruby, and saves the result without locking. Two concurrent registration attempts for the same blocked email can both read N and save N+1, recording only one of the two matches; an older request can also overwrite a newer `last_match_at`. Update the statistics atomically in the database or serialize these updates with a row lock so the recorded blocklist activity remains accurate.
